samples.lead: Choosing a sample opens its own project and walks you through CSV import → analysis → results and evidence, so you can see what Insight shows — and what it does not conclude — before using your own data.
samples.mixed.caution: Population (2020) and establishments (2016, 2021, private only) differ in timing and definition. The three memos are fictional.
samples.mixed.learn: Evidence from several sources, the limits that different survey years and definitions put on comparison, and the data a decision would still need (rent, trade area).
samples.mixed.question: Can population alone decide a candidate area? What do establishment counts add, and what is still missing?
samples.mixed.title: Combine population and establishment counts: what can and cannot be compared
samples.population.caution: Census values are 1 October snapshots taken every five years. A difference between two points does not explain why it changed.
samples.population.learn: The differences the actual census values show (with source, unit and reference date), and what two points in time cannot tell you: the path in between and the reasons for change.
samples.population.question: How did the population of three cities in Ibaraki (Mito, Hitachiota, Tsukuba) change between the 2015 and 2020 censuses?
samples.population.title: Look at population change in Japanese official statistics
samples.previewNote: Card descriptions explain each sample before analysis. They are not results; results appear only after you run an analysis.
samples.provenance.title: Source, retrieval and transformation record
samples.shop.caution: Entirely fictional data. It does not describe any real shop's sales or reputation.
samples.shop.learn: Observations tied to quoted source text, competing explanations (a changed sales definition, shorter opening hours) and data that was never collected (returns, visits).
samples.shop.question: For the recorded sales increases and decreases, what can be explained and what is still unknown?
samples.shop.title: Find what changed in fictional shop records — and what is still missing
